Wrote parse_pack over a strict YAML loader that refuses aliases, merge keys and duplicate keys, and closed the hole Zero named: every allow-list entry is a full pair, so `fly version upgrade` (which replaces the binary) no longer hides behind a one-word check.

Not counted toward quorum (same family as the author). Found three curl options the deny-list never named (--json=@path, --libcurl, --etag-save) and that `~` was not a path escape. Verified each against the parser before reporting, which is why all four were applied within the hour.

Cross-family. Found the class the first round had not: the pytest option list banned what IMPORTS and never asked what WRITES (--junitxml over a source file), `expect: regex:` compiled a pattern without asking its cost (measured 0.376s at 24 characters, quadrupling every two), and 500 nested YAML sequences escaped the outcome taxonomy entirely with an uncaught RecursionError.

DID NOT RUN. The vendor's cyber filter refused the request; the run completed its tool loop, printed an ERROR line and exited 0, which is exactly the shape that reads as a clean review if nobody looks at the body. Recorded as not-run rather than as agreement.

Cross-family, reframed as a completeness review of a validator rather than as an attack, and it ran. Seventeen accepted-but-not-read-only forms with documentation links for each, plus three YAML fail-open classes including the one that mattered most: an invisible character in a KEY makes the whole block absent. The largest single contribution in this pack.

Three rounds, one shape: a deny-list over a tool's options is a list of the dangerous ones somebody remembered. So the cure is uniform rather than seventeen entries — every option list is an allow-list (git's GLOBAL one empty), value-taking options must be glued with =, no argument may open its value with @, every path is resolved before it is judged, and invisible characters are refused in the whole file. Two findings declined as unfixable in a parser and written into the module as constraints PR-2 inherits.

detail: 1) `git log --format '%GS'` was executable: the %G check read only the FLAG token, so the separate-value spelling passed.
